title: Reliability Sprint Accelerator — Cross-Functional Activation Agenda
body:
Purpose and context:
This doc outlines a focused 6-week sprint accelerator to operationalize a prioritized set of service-level objectives (SLOs) across teams that touch the inference stack: serving-runtime, platform-engineering, observability, console, and solutions-eng. The goal is not full productization — it is to create repeatable activation patterns, telemetry primitives, and a first-wave playbook that product teams can reuse.

Why this sprint?
- We have multiple services with partial SLO definitions and inconsistent telemetry.
- Recent incidents highlighted gaps in error-rate attribution and unclear ownership for latency regressions that cross runtime and networking.
- A short, cross-team concentrated effort will reduce blast radius, clarify ramps, and produce artifacts (dashboards, alert rules, SLO docs, rollout checklist) that scale.

Scope (in/out):
In scope:
- Define 3 canonical SLOs for each target service (latency p95, request success rate, end-to-end tail latency for inference requests).
- Implement required tracing/span conventions for request flow across runtime -> router -> cache -> network.
- Create one shared dashboard per SLO with KT (knowledge transfer) notes and an alert-to-runbook mapping.
- Run a single canary rollout with rollback automation and metrics validation.

Out of scope:
- Full platform rollout to dedicated/private customers during this sprint.
- Large-scale refactors of the runtime internals (we may create tickets).

Key objectives (measurable):
1) Publish canonical SLO definitions and owner for 5 services by week 2.
2) Trace context propagation implemented for 80% of request paths by week 4.
3) Dashboards + alert rules + runbooks in prod-ish dashboards for the SLOs by week 5.
4) Successful canary exercise with automated rollback trigger validated in staging by end of week 6.

Stakeholders and responsibilities (high level):
- Eng:serving-runtime — implement and validate trace headers, measure server-side latency, instrument tokenization and KV cache spans. Owner: Luca Moreno.
- Eng:platform-engineering — routing rules for canary, deployment config for graded traffic, infra quotas. Owner: Priya Desai.
- Eng:observability — define metric names, dashboard templates, SLI computation queries, alert severity mapping. Owner: Nora Singh.
- Product:console-and-rollouts — surface SLO status in console, rollout UI knobs, telemetry links for customers. Owner: Ethan Walker.
- Solutions & SRE on-call — runbook edits, post-mortem templates, and incident play rehearsals. Owner: Jamal Robinson.
- Program lead — Samira Kaur (facilitate, unblock cross-team dependencies, coordinate release window).

Tentative 6-week timeline (sprint-week view):
Week 0 (pre-kickoff, 1 week before):
- Alignment meeting with product and sales for scope guardrails.
- Tag & triage existing SLO-related tickets.
- Prep staging environment window for canary.

Week 1: Define and agree
- Finalize canonical SLO definitions (owner, SLI, SLO target, measurement window, burn rate thresholds).
- Deliverable: SLO spec doc + sign-off from all owners.

Week 2: Telemetry primitives
- Observability creates SLI queries and dashboard templates.
- Runtime implements basic span annotations.
- Deliverable: dashboard drafts and test traces for end-to-end flow.

Week 3: Instrumentation and alerting
- Wire alerts to runbook stubs, define alert severities and notification routes (PagerDuty, slack).
- Run a tabletop for the top-2 alert fires.
- Deliverable: alert -> runbook document + runbook PRs.

Week 4: Canary prep
- Platform config for staged rollouts, traffic shaping, and throttling.
- Add canary guardrails (automated traffic diversion thresholds).
- Deliverable: canary plan, deployment manifests, rollback hooks.

Week 5: Canary execution (staging -> limited prod)
- Execute canary with pre-agreed validation checks.
- Observe, iterate, and capture gaps.
- Deliverable: canary report + updated playbook entries.

Week 6: Retro + handoff
- Consolidate artifacts, update Confluence playbook, add onboarding checklist for future product teams.
- Deliverable: handoff packet + proposed rollout timeline for production-wide adoption.

Acceptance criteria (what good looks like):
- Each target service has a named SLO doc with owner and measurement query in the monitoring repo.
- Dashboards render meaningful historical baseline for at least 7 days in staging and 30 days in prod where available.
- A canary was executed and rollback automation triggered in at least one simulated failure scenario.
- Post-sprint playbook includes a checklist with minimal runnable steps for a product team to adopt SLOs in 2 sprints.

Open questions / riskiest assumptions (notes to self):
- Assumption: tracing headers can be propagated without changing existing client SDK contracts. If incompatible, we need a shim layer that may push work beyond sprint scope.
- Question: Do we standardize on percentiles for latency (p95 vs p99) per-service or create per-customer visibility? Recommend p95 canonical, p99 as escalation.
- Risk: On-call paging volume could spike during canary; mitigation: set high initial thresholds and run with SRE in monitor mode.

Communication plan and cadence:
- Daily 15-minute standup (10:00 PST) for sprint participants — brief blockers only.
- Weekly cross-functional demo + sign-off on Friday afternoons.
- Slack channel: #rel-accelerator (create thread per week), ephemeral zoom for runbook tabletop.
- Weekly update email to leadership with top 3 metrics and one ask.

Artifacts to produce (minimum viable set):
- Canonical SLO spec (Confluence + repo markdown).
- Dashboard template + example for each SLO.
- Alert rules + runbooks checked into repo.
- Canary runbook + deployment manifests (k8s/terraform as needed).
- Post-sprint playbook and onboarding checklist.

Runbook sketch (example for latency SLO breach):
1) Alert triggers (severity P2) -> PagerDuty to SRE rotation.
2) First responder runs quick triage script (link in runbook) to identify bottleneck: runtime CPU, KV cache miss rate, or router backlog.
3) If KV cache miss > 20% in last 5m, backfill cache and reduce canary traffic.
4) If runtime p95 > threshold and CPU saturation observed, trigger traffic diversion and rollback using platform throttle.
5) Post-incident: capture timeline, update playbook with missing obs signals.

Operational checklist for product teams onboarding after sprint:
- Confirm owner and contact info.
- Ensure service exports the agreed metric names and trace headers.
- Create a service SLO page with SLI queries and historical baseline.
- Schedule a canary window and confirm on-call availability.

Metrics we will track during the accelerator (not exhaustive):
- Number of services with SLO docs completed
- Percent of request paths with propagated trace ids
- Mean time to detect (MTTD) for SLO breaches
- Mean time to mitigate (MTTM) for canary failures
- Number of dashboard alerts fired during canary (signal:noise)

Jira conventions and quick tags (please use when creating follow-ups):
- REL-ACC-<number> for accelerator work items
- REL-SLO-<service>-<short> for SLO definition tickets
- REL-OBS-<ticket> for observability implementation work

Next steps (immediate):
- Schedule 60m kickoff with all owners (calendar invite pending).
- Owners to add preliminary SLO drafts to the Confluence SLO workspace by EOD Wednesday.
- Observability to produce dashboard skeleton and share Prometheus/TSDB queries.

Notes and loose thoughts (informal):
- Keep the initial SLOs conservative — we want buy-in and fast wins.
- Consider a small incentives badge for teams that onboard within the next quarter (internal recognition).
- Could reuse parts of the Console UI to show SLO health per service; prototype during Week 2.

Attachments to add before handoff:
- Links to example alert queries (observability repo).
- Example trace snippets showing a clean end-to-end request.
- Staging canary runbook with step-by-step safe commands.

If you are reading this and want to help: please add your availability for the 6-week window, and post your preliminary SLO ideas in the Confluence page linked above.

-- end --
